issue.title: Complete concrete catalog models in shell --model and --next-model values
issue.description: Proposing bead: sase-1ss.1, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #3. Root cause is explicit: src/sase/completion/candidates/catalog_build.py::model_candidates returns _BUILTIN_MODEL_ALIASES only, and model_source_path returns None. The existing test pins exactly five aliases; this is an intentional feature extension, not a regression from Hydrogen. Project packaged models.yml with importlib.resources.files("sase").joinpath("llm_provider", "models.yml") without importing sase.llm_provider or sase.macro in the shell fast path. Retain all five aliases; offer concrete bare and provider-qualified values, including agy/Hydrogen and all other providers. Supply model_source_path cache invalidation, and classify --next-model as ValueKind.MODEL in the authoritative shared option taxonomy. Follow the Rust backend boundary if the classification belongs in core, including pin update when a binding changes. Cover lazy imports, candidates, cache invalidation, both options, and shell parity; regenerate affected grammar snapshots. Active sase-12o and its phase .1 cover loader/grammar freshness and preserve the candidate fast path; this distinct candidate-set expansion is not caused by that epic. Medium because the static-five-candidate root cause and implementation boundary are bounded.

task_type_fields.proposal: Extend shell model candidates from five aliases to manifest-backed concrete models and classify --next-model for model completion.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic sase-1ss explicitly excludes shell completion design changes and promises manifest-driven surfaces only.

issue.creation_reason: Proposed by sase-1ss.1 note #3; shell completion still returns only five size aliases although the manifest supplies concrete models to the prompt and editor surfaces.
